_comment: CONFIG, not declaration -- #727 split them, and `contributes` is on HarnessConfig rather than on the declaration because it says how this instance behaves when a folio LOADS it, not what it is. `loadContributions` reads it through `readHarnessConfig`, which resolves `<name>.config.json` from the instance root outward, so a dependency with no config file can contribute nothing however it is declared. That is why this file exists at all: folio-assistant-sci is a DEPENDENCY here rather than an instantiated harness, and it carries no `contentType` -- the instantiation marker the root's siblings carry is the file AT THE REPO ROOT, not one inside an instance's own directory.
_contributes_comment: THE FIRST REAL CONTRIBUTOR. `ContributionRegistry` (Phase 0.1 of #223) had no production consumer at all until this entry -- every reference outside schemas/contributions.ts was its own test, and a mechanism with no caller is free to be subtly wrong in ways no test shape catches (bean rfev). The module contributes the two elaboration-cost QA checkers: `qa-checkers-cost.ts` moved here from cat-harness/content/pipeline/ because elaboration cost is a LEAN measurement, so the checker is this layer's tooling. The CRITERIA stay declared in core -- a criterion is a rule about content, a checker is the tooling that answers it, which is the owner's cut: 'f-a-core has high level processes only, no tooling'. Bean zlmp measured five core-or-harness runtime edges that `check:partition` cannot see because the target is named as a string; this drains the first of them.
